Depends on a hundred different things. How long are you going to live? That's a big question right there:)

Since there is no way to know, unless you are dying next week, you are probably going to need more than you think. What happens if you retire at age 60 - and live to be 112?

My personal opinion is it is best to go with income generating property - something that can keep pace with inflation AND continue to pay out adequately no matter how long you live. I know the system is designed for everyone to invest into pensions - but pensions are dependent upon the stability of the financial system itself, and that has proven to be less than reliable on more than one prior occasion.

I can not tell you how many people have found out when the time came to collect the pension that the pension was either gone, or would only pay out half or less, or that the accumulated value of the pension after inflation would only buy dog food. I can only tell you that this has happened to 10's of millions of people in the last two decades - and that theft of pension dollars is the biggest game in town.

Based on this observation, I personally feel it is best to not keep all eggs in the pension basket - rather, diversification, probably into income generating properties, as a hedge against inflation, and potential instability in the pension system / financial system. You need income coming in from more than one source, income that can grow with inflation - so that is most likely rents.
